title: NGC 6520 with Barnard 86
caption: The star cluster NGC 6520 and dust cloud Barnard 86, imaged by the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
credit: T. A. Rector/University of Alaska Anchorage and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Bright young stars of the open cluster NGC 6520 stand out against a crowded backdrop, with the dark dust cloud Barnard 86 nearby. The pair lies in the constellation Sagittarius, toward one of the densest parts of our Galaxy.

The background is packed with older stars from our Galaxy's central bulge. The cluster's young stars contrast with them sharply, and they probably formed out of gas connected to the neighboring dust cloud.

An open cluster is a loose group of stars born together from the same cloud of gas and dust. Dark clouds like Barnard 86 are dense enough to block the light of the stars behind them, so they appear as shadowy shapes against the starry background. Seeing a young cluster sitting beside such a cloud hints at where its stars may have come from.

understand.summary: The Blanco 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic II camera recorded this in visible and near-infrared light. B is shown in blue, V in green, I in orange and hydrogen-alpha in red.

explore: The image was taken on June 24th, 2007 with NSF's Blanco 4-m telescope at Cerro Tololo. It was released during 'Around the World in 80 Telescopes', a webcast held on April 3-4, 2009, as part of the 100 Hours of Astronomy during the International Year of Astronomy 2009.
